The petitioners have filed this petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1989, claiming the compensation of Rs.35,00,000/- from the respondents with regard to the death of R.Nandan, in the road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case of the petitioners as follows:

sentences.text: On 29.07.2021 at about 09.15 p.m., when the deceased R.Nandan, was proceeding as a pillion rider on the Bajaj Pulsor motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-53-EZ-3807, near Attibele bus stop, Sulibele, Hoskote Taluk, Bengaluru, at that time, the rider of the said motor cycle rode the same with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to road side electric pole, due to which, R.Nandan and rider fell down and sustained injuries.

Immediately after the accident, deceased was shifted to Silicon city hospital, Hoskote, where he was taken first aid treatment, then, he was shifted to Janapriya hospital, Bengaluru, where he was admitted as an inpatient,undergone several investigations, even though the best efforts and treatment given by the doctors, R.Nandan was died on 30-07-2021.

Later after conducting post- mortem in the Govt., hospital, Hoskote, the dead body was handed over to the petitioners and they have performed the last rites and obsequies of the deceased by spending Rs.4,00,000/- towards medical, transport, funeral and death ceremony.
3. It is stated that, the deceased was working as a Mechanic and earning Rs.20,000/- per month.

The deceased was the only bread earner of their family and due to his death, the petitioners are undergoing mental shock and agony, lost love and affection of their son and facing great financial difficulties.
It is further stated that the accident in question was due to the rash and negligence on the part of the rider of the Bajaj Pulsor motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-53-EZ-3807.
Hence, the respondent No.2 being the owner and respondent No.1 being the Insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
4. On service of notice, respondent No.2 remained absent and placed exparte.
The respondent No.1 has appeared before the court through counsel and filed written statement.
5. The 1st respondent in its objection statement has denied all the petition averments and contended that the petition itself is not maintainable either on facts or law.
It has denied the age, income and occupation of the deceased.
It has also denied the amount spent towards the medical and funeral expenses of the deceased.

Further admitted the issuance insurance policy in respect of the offending vehicle Bajaj Pulsor motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-53-EZ-3807 and liability if any is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy, provision of MV Act, valid and effective driving licence held by the rider of the offending vehicle.
Respondent also seeks protection under section 147 and 149(2) of M.V. Act.

It has also contended deceased himself riding the motorcycle and died due to self accident and Arunkumar was falsely implicated by the petitioners colluding with the owner of the motorcycle and the police as rider to get compensation.
It has also contended that owner and jurisdictional police have not complied the Sec.134(c) and Sec.158(6) of M.V. Act.
It has denied the alleged negligence of the rider of the offending vehicle.
Further contended that the compensation and interest claimed by the petitioners are excessive and exorbitant.
Hence on all these grounds, it has sought for dismissal of the petition.

6. Based on the pleadings, my predecessor in office has framed following issues:-

2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so, to what extent and from whom?
3. What order or Award?

Issue No.1 ... In the affirmative, Issue No.2 ... Partly in the affirmative, Issue No.3 ...

As per final order For the following:
REASONS 10. ISSUE NO.1 : It is the case of the petitioners that, on 29.07.2021 at about 09.15 p.m., when the deceased R.Nandan, was going as a pillion rider on the Bajaj Pulsor motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-53-EZ-3807, near Attibele bus stop, Sulibele, Hoskote Taluk, Bengaluru, at that time,
the rider of the said motor cycle rode the same with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to road side electric pole, due to which, R.Nandan and rider fell down and sustained injuries.
Immediately after the accident, deceased was shifted to Silicon city hospital, Hoskote, where he was taken first aid treatment, then, he was shifted to Janapriya hospital, Bengaluru, where he was admitted as an inpatient,undergone several investigations, even though the best efforts and treatment given by the doctors, R.Nandan was died on 30-07-2021.

It is specifically urged that, the accident happened because of the rash and negligent act of the offending vehicle rider and as such the respondents are liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.

11. In order to substantiate the contentions of the petitioners, the petitioner No.1 stepped into the witness box and filed his affidavit-in-lieu of oral examination-in-chief as PW1 and got marked F.I.R,
F.I.S, spot mahazar, sketch, inquest report, IMV report, charge sheet, PM report and lab reports, as S.N. Rajanna vs Liberty General Insurance Co. Ltd on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/9700059/
4 per Ex.P1 to Ex.P9.

sentences.text: In support of his version he has examined the 3 witnesses as Pw2 to 4 who are the Mro's of the hospitals and eye witness of the accident, which the deceased has taken treatment.

12. On the other hand, the Respondent No.1 has taken contention is that deceased himself was riding the motorcycle and died due to self accident and Arunkumar was falsely implicated by the petitioners colluding with the owner of the motorcycle and the police as rider to get compensation.
In support of their version the Respondent No.1 company has examined two witnesses as Rw1 and Rw2, got marked Ex.R1 and 2 and also R2(a).
The petitioners are bestowed with the burden to prove the specific assertions in the light of oral and documentary proof.
13. This issue revolves round the sphere and ambit as to the alleged rash and negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The factum of negligence has to be proved like any other fact in issue.
Before dwelling into analyzing the factum of alleged negligence, it is relevant to have the conceptual aspects pertaining to factum of negligence.
There are four basic elements that a person has to fulfill in order to do a negligent act.

These elements are as follows:
Duty: For committing a negligent act, there must be some duty on the part of the defendant.
Here it is important to understand whether the defendant has taken legal duty of care towards the plaintiff.
Breach of Duty:
After fulfilling the first criteria the plaintiff must prove that the defendant has breached the legal duty imposed on him/her.
It talks about the breach of duty on the part of the defendant which he/ she is expected to do as he/ she has some legal duty towards the plaintiff.
The action of causing something: It means that the damage caused to the plaintiff is due to the act of the defendant.
Here the defendant may do an act which is not expected from him/her or the defendant may be negligent in not doing an act which was expected from him/ her.
Damages: At last what matters is, there must be some damage/injury that is caused to the plaintiff and this damages should be the direct consequence of the defendant's act.

Negligence means a breach of duty caused by omission to do something which has reasonable man guide by those consideration which ordinarily regulated conduct of human affairs would do which a prudent man would not do.
In common prevalence negligence connoted to the want of proper care and the rashness conveys the idea of recklessness or the doing of an act without due consideration.

14. According to the version of petitioners the accident happened near Attibele bus stop, Sulibele,
Hoskote Taluk, Bengaluru, when the rider of the motor cycle bearing Reg.No. KA-53-EZ-3807 rode the same with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner at that time a dog came across the road to avoid the dog, he has dashed to road side electric pole, due to which, accident occurred.

It is S.N. Rajanna vs Liberty General Insurance Co. Ltd on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/9700059/
5 pertinent to note that, the criminal law was set in motion on the same day of accident as per Ex.P.2.
Ex.P.1 FIR has its germane in Ex.P.2.

sentences.text: The document which sheds light on the factum of negligence are Ex.P.3 being the Spot Mahazar and Ex.P4 Sketch prepared at the time of mahazar.

On close perusal of the Ex.P.3 and Ex.P4 it reflects that deceased was proceeding as a pillion rider on the Bajaj Pulsor motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-53-EZ-3807, near Attibele bus stop, Sulibele, Hoskote Taluk, Bengaluru, the rider of the bike rode his bike in high speed and negligent manner, the rider of the said motor cycle to avoid the dog which was came across the road, he has dashed to road side electric pole.
The said factum is also fortified with the IMV report.
If the rider of the Bajaj Pulsor motorcycle rode the vehicle in a normal speed by observing moments of the vehicles and also animals, then he would certainly avoid the accident.
Added more the contents of Ex.P.6 which is the IMV report itself discloses that there are no mechanical defects whatsoever in the offending vehicle.
Further more even the chargesheet as per Ex.P7 was also filed as against the rider of the Bajaj Pulsor motor cycle.

When such is the case having regard to Ex.P.3 and 4 coupled with Ex.P.7 charge sheet it is crystal clear that, the accident happened because of rash and negligence riding of the rider of the Bajaj Pulsor motorcycle.

15. The Respondent has contended that, deceased himself riding the motorcycle and died due to self accident and Arunkumar was falsely implicated by the petitioners colluding with the owner of the motorcycle and the police as rider to get compensation, in support of their version they relied on evidence of the RW1 and Rw2 and Ex.P2 and Ex.P2(a).

In the cross- examination Rw1 has admits that "It is true to suggested that after the accident immediately rider and pillion rider of the bike shifted and admitted in Srisairanga Hospital and further admits that "it is true to suggested that in Ex.P15 and 16 mentioned that Nandan is the pillion rider and Arunkumar is the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-53-EZ-3807".
These admissions and also on perusal of the Ex.P15 and 16 which were the MLC register extract and police intimation it is clearly mentioned the said facts.
Rw1 in his cross-examination has deposed that he has not involved in the investigations conducted by their investigation team.
16. As per the version of the Respondent No.1, Rw2 is the investigator, they collected the information regarding the accident through him.
In the cross-examination Rw2 also admits that ' it is true all the police documents and hospital records deceased is the pillion rider and Arunkumar is the rider of the motorcycle.
He further admits that he has not inquired the eyewitness of the accident as per police record and also rider and owner of the offending motorcycle.
The said Rw2 further deposed that 'in video recording there is no information about when and where accident occurred and number of the offending vehicle'.
Further deposed that there is no information about which vehicle caused the accident in the Ex.R2(a)".
As per the said deposition of the Rw1 and 2 also documents are contradictory to each one and also there is no information which vehicle accident caused.
Hence, the contention taken by the Responden No.2 is not believable.

17. It is necessary to reassert that in a claim for compensation filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is expected to prove the incident on basis of principle of preponderance of probabilities and the view taken by this Court is fortified by the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others which is reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.

Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal S.N. Rajanna vs Liberty General Insurance Co. Ltd on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/9700059/
6

entities.text: Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal S.N. Rajanna vs Liberty General Insurance Co. Ltd on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 has observed
that, it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.

Further the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Krishnappa and another reported in 2001 ACJ 1105, where the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka considering the fact that the rider of the offending vehicle was not examined to prove any contributory negligence on the part of scooterist held that the accident had occurred due to rash or negligent driving by the driver of the offending van.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Krishnappa and another reported in 2001 ACJ 1105
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Even in the instant case the rider of the motorcycle is not examined to show that there was no negligence on his part and even otherwise the IO, as already observed, has clearly opined that the accident occurred only due to the fault of the rider of the motorcycle and he was charge sheeted.
18. Further though PW.1 and PW.4 were cross examined by respondent No.1 counsel at length

,
nothing is elicited from their mouth with regard to the negligence on the part of rider of the motor cycle and on the other hand the petitioners with the help of Ex.P3, P4 and Ex.P6 coupled with Ex.P7 clearly demonstrated that there is a negligence on the part of offending vehicle rider.
Viewed from any angle this court does not find any reason to distrust the version of the petitioners herein.
The discussion supra makes it is abundantly clear that, the accident occurred solely due to the rash negligent riding of the Bajaj Pulsor motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-53-EZ-3807 by its rider.
As such, this Tribunal answers issue No.1 In the Affirmative.
19. Issue No.2:

While answering issue No.1, I have already observed that the death of R.Nandan, was occurred due to rash and negligent riding by the rider of offending vehicle Bajaj Pulsor motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-53-EZ-3807.
20.

The petitioners have contended that the deceased was was Mechanic and earning Rs.20,000/-
per month.
The petitioners have not produced any document to show the income of the deceased.
Therefore, in the absence of any evidence with regard to the income of the deceased, the court has to take into consideration the notional income.
Considering the work of the deceased and year of the accident is 2021, I deem it just and reasonable to take the notional income of the deceased at Rs.15,000/- per month.
21. It is stated that the deceased was aged 20 years at the time of the accident.
To prove the age of the deceased, PW.1 has produced the notarized copy of Aadhaar card of the deceased at Ex.P12 which shows the date of birth as 18-04-2001.
The accident was occurred in the year 2021.

Hence,
the age of the deceased at the time of accident was 20 years.

As such, the proper multiplier applicable to the case on hand is '18'.
22.

As per the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court reported in 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC) (National Insurance Company Limited Vs Pranay Sethi and others), if the person died in the motor accident, the income S.N. Rajanna vs Liberty General Insurance Co. Ltd on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/9700059/
7 with respect to the future prospect has to taken into consideration while awarding compensation.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The Hon'ble Apex Court has provide the chart for age of the deceased and percentage for future prospects in between below the age of 40 years 40%, 40 years to 50 years 25% and 50 to 60 years 10%.
The deceased is not a permanent Employee and not a fixed salary person and he died at the age of 20 years.
Therefore, in this case, 40% income has to be taken into consideration for future prospects.

As such, 40% is added to the income of the deceased, then it comes to Rs.21,000/- p.m.
(Rs.15,000/- + 6,000/- i.e. 40%).
The deceased died leaving behind 2 dependents and he was a bachelor.

As per principle laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarala Verma Case, 50%(1/2) of his income is required to be deducted towards his personal expenses which comes to Rs.10,500/-
p.m.(Rs. 21,000 - Rs.10,500 = Rs.10,500/-).
23. The income of the deceased is taken as Rs.10,500/- p.m. and the multiplier '18' is applied, then the loss of dependency comes to Rs.22,68,000/- (Rs.10,500 X 12 X 18).

Considering the above facts,
this Tribunal deems it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.22,68,000/- under the head of loss of dependency.
24. In this case, petitioner No.1 and 2 are the father and brother of the deceased.

As per the decision reported in (2018) 12 SCC 130 between Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others, the petitioners are entitled for filial consortium, as the filial consortium is the right of the parents and family members to compensation in the case of an accidental death of a child.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: An accident leading to the death of a child causes great shock and agony to the parents and family of the deceased.
The greatest agony for a parent is to lose of their child during their lifetime.
Children are valued for their love, affection, companionship and their oral in the family unit.
Therefore, petitioner No.1 and 2 are entitled for Rs.44,000/- each under the head of Filial consortium.

25. Further, as law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex court in National Insurance company Vs. Pranay Sethi and others, the compensation towards loss to the estate, funeral expenses and consortium to be awarded.

entities.text: National Insurance company Vs. Pranay Sethi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence this Tribunal award Rs.16,500/- towards loss to estate and Rs.16,500/- towards funeral expenses as enhanced at the rate of 10% on every 3 years.

 Compensation heads Compensation  amount  1. Towards loss of Rs.22,68,000/-

In all the petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.23,89,000/-.
27.
As regards the apportionment of the compensation, petitioners No.1 and 2 are father and brother of the deceased.

Therefore out of the total compensation, the petitioners No.1 and 2 are entitled for compensation at the ratio of 75:25.
28.
The petitioners are claiming interest on the compensation amount.
The respondent No.1 has denied the same.

Our Hon'ble High Court in the case rendered in Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another (MFA.No.100090/2014 C/W MFA.No.25107/2013 dated 07.03.2018), has held that in the absence of any other law relating to interest on judgments, the MACT has to follow the provisions of Sec.34 of C.P.C and awarded interest @ 6% per annum.

sentences.text: Considering the aforesaid decision, I deem it proper to award interest at 6% per annum on the above compensation amount.
29. Liability:

Regarding fixation of liability is concerned, I have already observed that the accident was taken place due to the negligence on the part of the rider of Bajaj Pulsor motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-53-EZ-3807.
It is not in dispute that 2 nd respondent is the owner of the offending vehicle.
The respondents have not proved the breach of any of the policy conditions.
Hence, 2nd respondent being the owner and 1 st respondent being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
The 1st respondent shall indemnify the 2nd respondent in payment of compensation amount.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.2 Partly in the Affirmative.
30. Issue No.3:

In view of my findings on issues No.1 and 2, I pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is allowed in part with cost.

The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.23,89,000/- (Rupees Twenty three lakhs eighty nine thousand only) with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.1 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.

On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
Petitioner No.1 - 75% Petitioner No.2 - 25% Out of the share amount of Petitioner No.1 and 2 a sum equal to 40% shall be deposited in their respective names in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of their choice for a period of 2 years and the remaining 60% shall be released to them through E- S.N. opennyai_summary.facts: The petitioners have filed this petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1989, claiming the compensation of Rs.35,00,000/- from the respondents with regard to the death of R.Nandan, in the road traffic accident.
opennyai_summary.issue:
Whether the petitioners prove that the deceased Sri.R.Nandan has died int eh road traffic accident occurred on 29-07-2021 at about 9.15 p.m., near Attibele bus top,
Sulibele, Hosakote Taluk, Bangalore district to the rash and negligent riding fo the rider of the Bajaj Pulsor motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-53-EZ-3807?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so, to what extent and from whom?
3. What order or Award?

As per final order For the following:
REASONS 10. ISSUE NO.1 : It is the case of the petitioners that, on 29.07.2021 at about 09.15 p.m., when the deceased R.Nandan, was going as a pillion rider on the Bajaj Pulsor motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-53-EZ-3807, near Attibele bus stop, Sulibele, Hoskote Taluk, Bengaluru, at that time,
the rider of the said motor cycle rode the same with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to road side electric pole, due to which, R.Nandan and rider fell down and sustained injuries.
Immediately after the accident, deceased was shifted to Silicon city hospital, Hoskote, where he was taken first aid treatment, then, he was shifted to Janapriya hospital, Bengaluru, where he was admitted as an inpatient,undergone several investigations, even though the best efforts and treatment given by the doctors, R.Nandan was died on 30-07-2021.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The factum of negligence has to be proved like any other fact in issue.
Before dwelling into analyzing the factum of alleged negligence, it is relevant to have the conceptual aspects pertaining to factum of negligence.
There are four basic elements that a person has to fulfill in order to do a negligent act.
These elements are as follows:
Duty: For committing a negligent act, there must be some duty on the part of the defendant.
After fulfilling the first criteria the plaintiff must prove that the defendant has breached the legal duty imposed on him/her.
The action of causing something: It means that the damage caused to the plaintiff is due to the act of the defendant.
Negligence means a breach of duty caused by omission to do something which has reasonable man guide by those consideration which ordinarily regulated conduct of human affairs would do which a prudent man would not do.
In common prevalence negligence connoted to the want of proper care and the rashness conveys the idea of recklessness or the doing of an act without due consideration.
Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal S.N. Rajanna vs Liberty General Insurance Co. Ltd on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/9700059/
6
The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.
Even in the instant case the rider of the motorcycle is not examined to show that there was no negligence on his part and even otherwise the IO, as already observed, has clearly opined that the accident occurred only due to the fault of the rider of the motorcycle and he was charge sheeted.
,
nothing is elicited from their mouth with regard to the negligence on the part of rider of the motor cycle and on the other hand the petitioners with the help of Ex.P3, P4 and Ex.P6 coupled with Ex.P7 clearly demonstrated that there is a negligence on the part of offending vehicle rider.
Considering the work of the deceased and year of the accident is 2021, I deem it just and reasonable to take the notional income of the deceased at Rs.15,000/- per month.
Therefore, in this case, 40% income has to be taken into consideration for future prospects.
24. In this case, petitioner No.1 and 2 are the father and brother of the deceased.
As per the decision reported in (2018) 12 SCC 130 between Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others, the petitioners are entitled for filial consortium, as the filial consortium is the right of the parents and family members to compensation in the case of an accidental death of a child.
An accident leading to the death of a child causes great shock and agony to the parents and family of the deceased.
The greatest agony for a parent is to lose of their child during their lifetime.
Children are valued for their love, affection, companionship and their oral in the family unit.
opennyai_summary.arguments: 17. It is necessary to reassert that in a claim for compensation filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is expected to prove the incident on basis of principle of preponderance of probabilities and the view taken by this Court is fortified by the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others which is reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Therefore, petitioner No.1 and 2 are entitled for Rs.44,000/- each under the head of Filial consortium.
Hence this Tribunal award Rs.16,500/- towards loss to estate and Rs.16,500/- towards funeral expenses as enhanced at the rate of 10% on every 3 years.
Total Rs.23,89,000/-
In all the petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.23,89,000/-.

Considering the aforesaid decision, I deem it proper to award interest at 6% per annum on the above compensation amount.
29. Liability:
It is not in dispute that 2 nd respondent is the owner of the offending vehicle.
Hence, 2nd respondent being the owner and 1 st respondent being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
The 1st respondent shall indemnify the 2nd respondent in payment of compensation amount.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.2 Partly in the Affirmative.
30. Issue No.3:
In view of my findings on issues No.1 and 2, I pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is allowed in part with cost.
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.23,89,000/- (Rupees Twenty three lakhs eighty nine thousand only) with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.1 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.
On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
Petitioner No.1 - 75% Petitioner No.2 - 25% Out of the share amount of Petitioner No.1 and 2 a sum equal to 40% shall be deposited in their respective names in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of their choice for a period of 2 years and the remaining 60% shall be released to them through E- S.N. Rajanna vs Liberty General Insurance Co. Ltd on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/9700059/
9 payment on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioners are at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on the deposit amount from time to time.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
